We absolutely love WagWear for our pup and actually went to NYC specifically to visit the store and shop for him. So naturally, we were really excited to finally experience the brand in person.

Unfortunately, the in-store experience was… quite the opposite of what we expected from a pet brand. The lady at the counter was pretty rude and unfriendly, and we definitely got the impression that she had already decided we weren’t going to buy anything. Nothing says “welcome to our store” quite like being made to feel like you’re wasting someone’s time. 🙃

And yes, we DID end up purchasing — because we genuinely love WagWear. But the irony didn’t stop there. Considering this is the only WagWear store in NYC, we were honestly shocked by how little inventory was available. A lot of the things we wanted were simply not there, which made the trip feel pretty underwhelming.

For a brand that is all about making pets look cute and happy, the store itself felt surprisingly cold and unwelcoming. 🥲 We really wanted this to be a fun WagWear experience for our pup, especially since we went out of our way to visit.

We love the products, but unfortunately, the customer service and inventory at this location left a lot to be desired. At this point, we’d rather buy from our local pet stores in Toronto, where the experience is actually warm, welcoming, and feels like they’re happy to have you there.

I’ve purchased Wagwear shoes four times now, my dog won’t wear any other brand, so that says a lot about the comfort and fit. However, after continued use, I’ve noticed some issues that I really wish would be addressed.

The biggest concern is functionality. On a recent trip to New York, my dog wore the shoes all day, but dirt still got inside and his paws ended up dirty anyway. If debris is getting into the shoes that easily, it makes me question how much protection they’re actually providing. I’d much rather see improvements in the design to better seal out dirt and debris, rather than new colors or “sport mode” versions.

I also visited the Wagwear store in New York and was honestly disappointed with the experience. There was no greeting - not even acknowledgment of my dog - which felt off for a brand centered around pets. It didn’t feel welcoming, and the overall vibe didn’t match what I expected.

Lastly, the brand’s social media presence seems to have shifted. It feels less focused on dogs and their well-being than it used to, which is part of why I originally supported the brand.

I’ve been a repeat customer, but these experiences make me question whether I’ll continue supporting Wagwear moving forward. I really hope the brand refocuses on product performance and customer (and dog!) experience.

Im writing a NEW review. This is based on the service I recieved at the Wagwear store in NYC on 11th street on Wednesday Jan. 28th 2026. First let me state I love Wagwear products, I frequently buy the shoes & Jackets for my dogs. Anytime I'm stopped on the street regarding my dogs shoes and jackets I always give rave reviews! They're my favorite dog brand. With that being said, my dog lost one shoe and while I could of ordered one online, I needed it right away with the snow storm we had. I called the store, no one answered so I followed the directions and left a voicemail. No one called me back like the voicemail said they would. 5 days passed and still, no email, no text, no call back, nothing. So I decided to travel way downtown on mass transit from the Heights it took about an hour and 20 minutes. When we entered the store and told the young lady we needed just one shoe because our dog lost only one (of a brand new set we'd just bought this month), she was VERY dismissive off the bat, and she said we dont sell them loose, even though she grabbed a bag of loose shoes from behind a wall. She didnt bother to reach inside the bag or look. She didnt offer to order anything for us, she was very persistant in making us feel like our patronage was unwanted! We felt we (myself & my husband) were treated very poorly and brushed off. Im not sure if it was because we were there to buy just one shoe BUT IF THEY HAD ANSWERED THE PHONE, emailed texted or called us back like the voicemail said someone would, it would of saved me the time wasted going to the store in person. Honestly, im highly offened because im always recommending this brand and posting pics of my dogs with the gear and to be treated less than by a young lady who is of color like myself and my husband infront of other customers was embarrassing and humiliating!! I recognize its not the brands fault so I will continue to order but I will definitely let people know about the terrible sales girl at the store and urge them not to go in person. Such a shame that a great brand would have shitty help at their store! And poor customer service as far as contacting customers. I'm livid!!! WAGWEAR – New York, NY (48 E 11th Street)

Wagwear makes excellent dog shoes — the product itself is great. Unfortunately, the customer service at this specific location is consistently terrible, and after three separate visits, I feel compelled to speak up.

This was my third time visiting the 48 E 11th Street store. During my first visit, a younger sales associate was pleasant and helpful. However, even then, an older woman wearing a black sweater was sarcastic and rude.

On my second visit, that same woman attempted to rush me out of the store because another dog she preferred was present. I walked out, thought about it, and returned to state that I would be putting my dog’s shoes on in-store. I still spent over $100 that day, yet I was treated as though my presence was an inconvenience.

Today, on my third visit, I returned hoping there would be a change. There wasn’t. I came in with my son to purchase shoes for my golden doodle puppy. Both older women working were dismissive and offered very minimal help. They seemed uncomfortably concerned about my puppy, as if he were going to do something wrong — despite the fact that their dog (a miniature pinscher) approached my dog first, which they then quickly moved away. This interaction made me feel uncomfortable and singled out.

Based on repeated experiences, I seriously doubt this behavior is applied equally to all customers. I personally witnessed noticeably different energy and attention given to dogs and customers they seemed to favor during a previous visit.

To make matters worse, when I asked a simple question about whether the store offers any trade-in or discount options for previously purchased shoes (due to an impulsive buy), the woman in the black sweater responded sarcastically: “Well, if you grow out of pants, stores don’t take those back.”
This comment was unnecessary, rude, and incorrect. When I corrected her — as some stores do offer such programs — she responded defensively rather than professionally.

Overall, the tone, dismissiveness, and sarcasm from the staff — particularly the older employees — create an unwelcoming and tense environment. As a person of color, the treatment felt uncomfortable and outdated, with an edge that has no place in retail today.

This store needs management involvement and serious staff retraining. Great products do not excuse disrespectful or biased customer service. I love the shoes, but I will not continue supporting a location where I feel unwelcome and disrespected.
